entities.summary: Philip of Swabia, styled Philip II in his charters, was a member of the House of Hohenstaufen and King of Germany from 1198 until his assassination on June 28, 1208. Born into a prominent noble family, Philip was the son of Duke Frederick I of Swabia and the grandson of Emperor Henry V. He ascended to the throne following the death of his uncle, Emperor Henry VI, and faced numerous challenges, including the ongoing conflict with the Holy Roman Empire's rival claimants. Despite these pressures, Philip implemented various reforms, expanded the empire's borders, and promoted the interests of his family's dynasty. His reign was marked by a series of diplomatic maneuvers and military campaigns, including the Battle of Wiborn, which secured his position as king. However, Philip's reign was cut short by his assassination, which sparked a succession crisis and led to the eventual coronation of his cousin, Frederick II, as Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire. Philip's legacy as a skilled politician and military leader has endured, with his reign serving as a testament to the Hohenstaufen dynasty's influence in medieval Europe.
